attempts.label: CRCNS:aa-4
attempts.entry_title: Time-varying information of avian auditory neurons for communication calls (Elie and Theunissen 2019)
attempts.summary: None of the paper's main findings could be tested in this data: that zebra finch auditory neurons are as informative about calls in their sustained response as at onset, that a fixed rate code captures only part of that information, and that a categorical information index shows how invariantly units respond to calls of one type. The files do not mark the 404 single units the paper analyses, chosen by a decoding step it does not describe, and hold no recording-site locations. The units' Poisson statistics were blocked for the same reason. Of the Figure 1 model neurons, only the temporal one is published, and on it the rate and information estimates met the paper's values.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Elie and Theunissen (2019) on CRCNS data set aa-4, which holds the spike times of zebra finch auditory units to the vocal repertoire. The files do not mark the 914 single units or the 404 units the paper analyses, and hold no anatomical locations, so the population claims are blocked; the simulated model neuron of Figure 1 is tested on the paper's code repository.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Elie and Theunissen (2019) from CRCNS aa-4

outcomes.statement: The analysis uses 404 of the 914 isolated single units, those from which call type could be decoded above chance in the authors' earlier study.
outcomes.source: Methods, Neurophysiological and histological procedures, last paragraph
outcomes.quote: The data of neural responses from 404 out of 914 isolated single units were used in this study. The 404 neurons were selected based on a prior analysis that showed that this subset of units were not only auditory but also contained information about call-types
outcomes.notes: Neither reading of the criterion can be carried out. Reading (a): the files hold no list or flag of the 404 units, and the data description and the 2015 paper (Elie and Theunissen 2015, read at PMC4347984) give none. Reading (b): the 2015 decoding starts from the 914 single auditory units, defined in the 2015 Methods and the data description by I_AR of at least 2.3 bits/s among spike-sorted units and a spike-snippet SNR above 5. The I_AR reading matches the authors': 1401 spike-sorted files of any sortType have a stored I_AR of at least 2.3 bits/s, the 1401 auditory spike-sorted units of the description. The files hold 1281 units labelled single (sortType single, or singl in three files), 1246 of them auditory. The SNR is not stored. Computed from the snippet files (.f32, one per site and protocol, every site having one for its call protocol; layout from CRCNSCode/h5_plot_one_spike.m in the archive) on the call-protocol snippets of 1452 of the 1453 spike-sorted units, the threshold of 5 leaves 461 auditory units (SNR reading A, the SD of each snippet's maximum minus minimum) or 274 (reading B, the SD of the snippet at the samples of the average's maximum and minimum), not 914; reading A leaves 772 at a threshold of 4 and 1120 at 3. So the data set does not hold 914 identifiable single units (expected 914, tolerance 0), and a selection of 404 could only be redone on a different base set. The main reason is the missing unit labels (metadata_insufficient); methods_underspecified is the block the criterion names.

outcomes.statement: Of the 404 units, 337 have at least one time point with significant stimulus cumulative information, and these 337 form the population analysed.
outcomes.source: Methods, Information theoretic calculations, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: categorical instantaneous and cumulative information were calculated on a restricted set of 337 neurons that presented at least one time point with a significant value of stimulus cumulative information (significant threshold set as 3 times the local error
outcomes.notes: Rests on the 404 units of units-404, which cannot be identified in the files (see units-404); blocked for the same reason. Even with the units, the locally adaptive KDE rates and their jackknife estimates alone were estimated in the notebook at more than 100 hours on one core (128 h in the executed run), before the Monte Carlo cumulative information, so the claim would also be too_large here.

outcomes.statement: Low-pass filtering at 50 Hz (10 ms bins) keeps 96.7% +- 6.9% of the coherence-based information of the spike trains, only 88 of 404 units lose more than 5%, and 98.8% +- 1.6% of the power of the KDE rates lies below 50 Hz.
outcomes.source: Methods, Time-varying spike rate estimation, paragraph 4; S1 Fig
outcomes.quote: Over all units, 96.7% ±6.9% (mean ± SD) of information was conserved by a lowpass filtering at 50Hz and only 88 out of 404 cells had information losses greater than 5%. ... On average across units, the cumulative power reached 98.8%±1.6% (mean ± SD) at 50Hz
outcomes.notes: Rests on the 404 units of units-404, which cannot be identified in the files (see units-404); blocked for the same reason. Variant on the 1246 auditory single units, deciding nothing: the coherence stored in the files (4 to 496 Hz) puts 65.8% +- 19.0% of I_AR below 50 Hz; nothing shows that the stored curve is the computation of S1 Fig, so this says nothing about the paper's 96.7%. The KDE power part needs the KDE rates, which are too large to compute here (see units-337), and was not computed.

outcomes.statement: For simulated Poisson neurons (rate, onset and temporal codes, 4 stimuli, 10 trials), the KDE recovers the model rates with an average error below 0.02 spikes/ms, the cumulative information approaches the 2-bit maximum, and the temporal neuron's peak instantaneous information is 0.5 bits.
outcomes.source: Results, Time-varying information for model neurons, paragraphs 2 and 3; Figure 1
outcomes.quote: over all stimuli and model neurons, the average error was less than 0.02 spikes/ms ... in the Temporal neuron ( Fig 1C & 1F ) a peak instantaneous information of 0.5 bits is expected as 1 out 4 stimuli will be almost perfectly discriminated
outcomes.notes: The paper's code repository holds one model cell (ModelCell_InfoCumInfo_Tutorial.mat), a temporal neuron: 4 stimuli, 10 trials, 400 ms, each stimulus driving a response at a different time. The rate and onset neurons of Fig 1 are not there, so the criterion's 'each model neuron' can be checked for one of three. On it all three conditions hold. The mean absolute difference between the KDE and the model rate is 0.009 spikes/ms (per stimulus 0.0075 to 0.0103; RMS 0.016), below 0.02. Under the paper's procedure, as its code runs it, the bias-corrected cumulative information reaches 1.982 bits (14 bins at or above 1.8, last bin 1.884; all 40 bins computed, largest error 0.234 bits, two bins at 5,000,000 samples), at least 1.8; the MATLAB tutorial's saved results with the same procedure give 1.981 and 1.894. The peak bias-corrected instantaneous information is 0.520 bits at 140 ms, within 0.5 +- 0.05. The simplified procedure (one set of 200,000 samples for all bins, jackknife set k for every stimulus) gives 1.928 bits and a peak of 0.519, and the model rates give a largest cumulative information of 1.990 bits (last bin 1.956) and a peak of 0.540. With independent draws per jackknife replicate, which is not the code's procedure, the cumulative information rises to 2.206 bits and ends at 0.803. The Python KDE matches the KDE saved by the MATLAB tutorial to 0.0004 spikes/ms on average (largest 0.0033).
deviations: Data, the paper's tutorial model cell only (data elsewhere, GitHub julieelie/PoissonTimeVaryingInfo at commit 978020328321c7ed83be12c0152bed85ec77e218); the rate and onset model neurons of Fig 1 are not published.

KDE, the Python port of ssvkernel in the adaptivekde package (1.2.0), in place of the MATLAB ssvkernel the paper cites (reference 42); its output matches the MATLAB KDE saved with the tutorial (mean difference 0.0004 spikes/ms).

Model rate, the tutorial's Input_Spike_count read as the mean count per 10 ms bin and divided by 10 for spikes/ms; its rows sum to 12.0, 11.0, 9.0 and 10.5 spikes per trial for the four stimuli, against 12.1, 8.3, 8.5 and 11.4 observed.

Cumulative and instantaneous information as the paper's code computes them (Methods, The cumulative information: 'Monte Carlo samples were chunked in groups of 100,000 samples ... Sampling stopped when the standard error was below 0.2 bits or at a max number of samples set to 5,000,000 samples. If the error at the maximum number of samples was greater than 0.6 bits ... the calculation was not performed for any successive time points'; Bias correction, NB = 20; cumulative_info_poisson_model_MCJK_wrapper.m, cumulative_info_poisson_model_calculus_MCJK.m and Tutorial_TimeVarying_Information.mlx at the pinned commit). Taken from the code, as the text does not give them: the jackknife sets are evaluated on the Monte Carlo samples drawn for the full data, each bootstrap pairs the jackknife sets of the stimuli at random, the error is the square root of the mean over bootstraps of the variance of the pseudo-values N I - (N-1) I_k, and the wrapper stops at 3 x 0.2 bits. NB = 20 follows the paper; the tutorial uses 10 for the cumulative and 100 for the instantaneous information.

findings.statement: The files do not mark the 914 single auditory units the data description and the paper report, nor the 404 units the paper analyses. 1281 h5 files are labelled single units (sortType), 1246 of them with stored I_AR of at least 2.3 bits/s, the 2015 auditory threshold. The spike-snippet SNR that defines a single unit is not stored; computed from the snippet files as the description defines it, the threshold of 5 leaves 461 or 274 of the 1401 auditory spike-sorted units (two readings of the definition), not 914. Without a list of units, none of the paper's population results can be repeated on its units.

The data description says the data set holds 688 multi-units and 914 single auditory units, one h5 file each. The files are 845 unsorted multi-unit files (sortType tdt) and 1453 spike-sorted files (named _ss): 1281 labelled single, 63 multi and 109 noise.
The anatomical area and the x, y, z coordinates of the recording sites, used in the paper's Table 1 and Figure 10, are not in the data set; only the electrode, site and array depths are stored.

The numbers of stimuli and trials differ from the stated ones. In the call protocol (groups Call, Call1, Call1c, Call2, Call3) single units have 115.3 stimuli on average (sd 34.2, 34 to 133) against the paper's 114 (sd 22, 34 to 123), and 90.7 call stimuli of the nine call types (34 to 110); over every group they have 121.9 stimuli (73 to 137) against the description's 144 (64 to 153). 1874 unit-stimulus pairs of the call protocol have 12 trials, against a stated maximum of 11. The other protocols in the files (Sel1 to Sel7, Mask1, STRF1), which also hold call stimuli, are not described.
Three h5 files store sortType as 'singl'; and the description's section on file organisation names a bird WhiBlu5896M, where the files and the summary say WhiBlu5396M.

The per-site .f32 files of spike waveforms are described only as the waveform of the action potentials. Their layout (18 float32 samples per spike, indexed from 1 by the spike_ids of the h5 files) is documented only by the plotting function h5_plot_one_spike.m in the archive's CRCNSCode.tar.gz. There is one per site and protocol; bird BlaBro09xxF has two files for site 4 and Call1 (1,956,253 and 33,047 snippets, named with _ and -).

paper_notes.statement: The paper selects its 404 units by a decoding analysis it does not describe, citing Elie and Theunissen 2015, and its code repository holds neither that selection nor the selection of the 337 units, the locally adaptive KDE step, the exponential fits or the CII. The single-unit SNR defined in the Methods, computed from the snippet files, does not recover the 914 units. Question for the authors: can the lists of the 914, 404 and 337 units be published, with the file names of the data set, and on which snippets and with which noise measure was the SNR computed?

The paper gives NB = 20 bootstraps of the jackknife for the error on information, while the tutorial of its code repository uses 10 for the cumulative and 100 for the instantaneous information. The text does not say that the jackknife sets are paired across stimuli at random in each bootstrap, nor that the jackknife sets are evaluated on the Monte Carlo samples of the full data; the code does both.

entries.name: elie-2019
entries.title: Time-varying information of avian auditory neurons for communication calls (Elie and Theunissen 2019)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Elie and Theunissen (2019) on CRCNS data set aa-4, which holds the spike times of zebra finch auditory units to the vocal repertoire. The files do not mark the 914 single units or the 404 units the paper analyses, and hold no anatomical locations, so the population claims are blocked; the simulated model neuron of Figure 1 is tested on the paper's code repository.
